resources.string: What have I got on today?
Everything runs on this phone, or on your own server.
Let Lin see messages that can be replied to, so it can write an answer. Replies never send on their own — Lin writes, you press send.
This sends immediately. There is no undo.
That reply could not be sent - the message may have been dismissed. Nothing went out.

Off by default. When on, Lin reads a finished conversation for lasting facts about you and writes them down without asking each time. Everything it keeps is listed under what Lin remembers, and you can delete any of it.

Hold the power button, or use your phone\'s assistant gesture, and Lin opens listening. Set it as your assistant below. In a car this reaches Lin over plain Bluetooth, where the voice-dial button summons the phone\'s assistant — but not through Android Auto, whose microphone button only ever calls Google\'s own assistant.
Answer out loud when spoken to
Typed questions are always answered in writing.
Replies stay on screen. In a car, a spoken question is still answered out loud.
Ask out loud, answered out loud; type, and it writes
No voices yet — the phone\'s speech engine is still starting, or has none installed.

Voices belong to the phone\'s speech engine rather than to Lin, so this opens its settings. Google\'s and Samsung\'s engines download extra voices there; a neural engine installed from elsewhere — a Piper or Sherpa-ONNX one, which runs on the phone and sounds far better — appears in the list above once it is the chosen engine. Anything marked “online” sends what Lin says to that engine\'s servers to be read out.

Opens your phone\'s own settings, where Lin appears under Digital assistant app. Android only lets you choose this yourself — and it goes back to whichever app came with the phone if Lin is uninstalled, so if summoning stopped working after a reinstall, this is why.

Your phone points at an older part of Lin, from before the panel existed — Android remembers the exact screen you picked, not just the app. Summoning still works, but it goes through the full app on the way. Pick Lin again below to have the panel open straight away.
Lin is the assistant on this phone.
Something else is the assistant, so the power button and the assistant gesture will not reach Lin.
This phone will not say which app is its assistant. If summoning Lin does nothing, this is the thing to set.
This phone has no assistant screen Lin can open. It is usually under Apps, then Default apps.

The same panel the power button summons. Worth trying if summoning does nothing: if it appears from here but not from the button, it is the setting above or the phone\'s own side-button and gesture settings, not Lin.

Where the bigger model runs. A LAN address at home, or a tunnel hostname from outside — either works, as long as it is the full URL. Pick what is actually running: the three speak different APIs, and pointing at the wrong one fails in a way that looks like the server being down.

Sent with every request, as Name: value — one per line, since a Cloudflare Access service token is two of them. This is also where an API key goes, as "Authorization: Bearer …". Worth setting if the server is reachable from the internet: Ollama and vLLM have no password of their own, so anyone who learns the address can use them.
Everything Lin has kept, newest first. Delete anything here and it is gone — it will not be recalled again.
Nothing yet. Lin writes something down when you ask it to remember.
This deletes all %1$d of them. It cannot be undone.
You asked Lin to remember this · %1$s
Lin kept this from a conversation · %1$s

The one thing Lin sends off your phone. To answer \u201cwhat is it doing outside\u201d it asks open-meteo.com — no account, no key — and all that goes is a pair of coordinates rounded to about a kilometre: the same weather, a different street. No name, no question, nothing else, and only when you ask about the weather.
Let Lin use your rough location
Lin can look up the weather where you are.
Index your photo library so Lin can find pictures by what is in them. It runs on this phone — nothing is uploaded, and no picture is copied. Thousands of photos take a while.

Android Auto\'s microphone button always calls Google\'s own assistant — no app can take it, and with Gemini not installed it does nothing at all. What does reach Lin in a car is the voice button over plain Bluetooth, and “Hey Lin” on the phone itself. Both need Lin to already be listening, and Android does not let an app start listening in the background — so the notification below is the one tap that starts it.
One tap starts Lin listening, without opening the app. Tap it before you set off.
Needed in a car, where the phone is locked while Android Auto runs. Off by default: it shows the conversation to whoever is holding the phone.
Lin fills the dialer in and you press call
Dials straight out while the phone is in car mode, fills the dialer in everywhere else
A misheard name rings somebody, with no tap in between
Your choice, not a guess. Deciding automatically needs a model that can judge which requests are hard, and that comes with delegation.
Works with no network and no server.
Uses the model picked below. Falls back to the phone when the server cannot be reached, and says so.
What the server already has pulled. The one you pick is what answers when "The server" is chosen above.
Fill in the address above, then check.
The server answered and has no models pulled yet. Pull one on the server — for example "ollama pull qwen3:8b" — then check again.
You picked %1$s, and the server does not have it any more. Choose one from the list.

Which app “play Stan by Eminem” should use. Lin will not guess: with nothing chosen it says so rather than opening whichever service it finds first. Whether the song starts playing or the app just opens on the search is up to the app — Lin checks what is actually playing afterwards and tells you which of the two happened.
No app on this phone says it can play music.
Working on the server — this can take a minute…
Lin answers with a model running on this phone, and there is not one here yet. %1$s is about %2$s GB — worth starting on Wi-Fi.
✓ Answering with this — tap to let Lin choose
Tap “Use this one” to pick which downloaded model answers. Without a choice, Lin picks the one suited to this phone.
Models are read from, and will be downloaded to:
Ollama\'s own API. Listens on 11434. No key unless you put a proxy in front of it.
vLLM\'s OpenAI-compatible API. `vllm serve` listens on 8000, and pasting the /v1 address from its README is fine. Usually no key.
Unsloth\'s OpenAI-compatible API. Use the port Unsloth printed, and put its sk-unsloth key in the header field below as "Authorization: Bearer sk-unsloth-…".
Not every server lists its models. If yours does not, type the model\'s name exactly as the server knows it — it will be used without checking.
Tap to open. Turn this off in settings to stop listening.
Tap to start listening for “Hey Lin”.

Lin listens for its name and opens when it hears it, even with the screen off. Off by default, and worth knowing why: this is not a wake-word chip — there is no ready-made model for “Hey Lin”, so Lin runs the phone\'s speech recogniser continuously and reads the words. It costs battery, and a notification stays up the whole time it is listening.
Lin can appear over other apps, so “Hey Lin” answers straight away.

Lin cannot appear over other apps — and Android will not let an app in the background open a window without that, whatever else it is doing. So “Hey Lin” will put what it heard in a notification to tap instead of answering hands-free.
Let Lin appear over other apps
A copy of what cannot be got back if this phone is lost: what Lin remembers, your training files, and your settings. Keep it somewhere other than this phone.

Models are not included — they are gigabytes and download again. Nor is the photo index, which rebuilds from photos still on the phone. The backup does contain your server address and any API key you entered.
Restoring adds to what is here and never deletes — a memory already held is skipped. Settings are replaced.

Lin keeps a copy of every conversation and packs them into a .jsonl file every %1$d. One conversation per line, in the messages format a trainer reads directly. Everything said to Lin is written to this phone in readable text — and a conversation that used a tool carries whatever the tool returned, which can include other people\'s messages and the contents of documents you gave it.
Turning this off stops new ones being recorded. It does not delete what is already here.
%1$d more and the next file is written.
No files yet — the first is written once there are %1$d conversations.
This deletes %1$d packed file(s) and %2$d conversations waiting to be packed. It cannot be undone, and they cannot be collected again.
Lin can read a document you give it, and write new ones. It cannot browse your storage — each file here is one you added or shared to Lin, and removing it takes that access away again.
Nothing yet. Add a PDF, a Word document or a text file — or share one to Lin from any app.
Lets Lin answer what you have on. Reading only — an event Lin creates opens in your calendar app with the fields filled in, and you save it, so Lin can never put anything in your week on its own.

Lin can work a question out before answering. Thinking is generated at the same speed as the answer, so it is paid for in waiting before the first word — useful for a question with steps in it, wasted on the time of day.
A real chain, and a real wait
The model on the server decides for itself how long to think; the level above only turns it on or off there.
Show how it worked this out
The last %1$d attempts closed before anything appeared, so this time Lin started with everything switched off. Nothing has been deleted.
Nothing was recorded, which is itself a clue: it means the app was stopped by the system rather than by an error in its own code, and running out of memory is the usual reason.
